components.notes: pnpm + Nx workspace root. CI runs pnpm run build:ci, then every packages/* vitest suite through nx run-many (scripts/ci-unit-tests.ts splits node vs browser packages; jsdom, no real browser). @sentry/bun runs via nx -p @sentry/bun with Bun installed. Plain pnpm test also runs @sentry/deno, which downloads Deno.
Published @sentry/server-utils; vitest run via the root nx test graph (Node Unit Tests).
Published @sentry/core; vitest run via the root nx test graph.
Published @sentry/nextjs; vitest run via the root nx test graph. The other ~45 packages/* SDKs are members of . below 0.02 each and are folded into the root.

Excluded from the root unit-test run; CI's Deno Unit Tests job does cd packages/deno && pnpm run build && pnpm run test. The test script downloads Deno (install:deno) and Deno type definitions (deno-types) unless present.

176 test applications; each is installed from npm against packed SDK tarballs (pnpm run build:tarballs first), some start DBs with docker compose, and assertions run in Playwright browsers. CI copies each app to a temp dir and runs pnpm test:build then pnpm test:assert per matrix entry.
CI runs pnpm run test (sharded) with working-directory set here, after the root build; DB suites start Docker containers (describeWithDockerCompose: Postgres, MySQL, Redis, mssql, etc.).
Playwright suites (chromium, firefox, webkit) against the built CDN bundles; needs the root build and build:bundle first.
setup.mjs builds and packs @sentry/core and @sentry/bundler-plugins, then installs each fixture's dependencies from npm before vitest runs.
Vitest suites that start workers locally with wrangler dev (workerd from node_modules).
Needs the Bun runtime on PATH (CI uses oven-sh/setup-bun, Bun 1.3.14 and 1.4).
Runs deno test suites then shared Node suites with vitest; the test script downloads Deno and Deno types when absent.
Not a pnpm workspace package; CI runs node dev-packages/browser-min-version-tests/run.mjs, which downloads Chromium 80 and drives it over CDP against the built bundles.
